correctness.rationale: Corollary 3.9 expresses each fixed-degree coefficient as a finite sum over partitions. Definition 2.5 makes every vertex multiplicity Laurent-polynomial in \(q^{1/2}\), and Proposition 2.6/Remark 2.7 give finiteness. The only displayed non-Laurent factors are \([\ell]_q^{-k_{\ell j}}\). Since \(\sum_{\ell}\ell k_{\ell j}=p_j\), one has \(k_{\ell j}\le\lfloor p_j/\ell\rfloor\), so \(D_p\) clears every denominator. Theorem A identifies the coefficient with the all-genus series after \(q=e^{iu}\). At a nontrivial primitive \(d\)-th root, each \([\ell]_q\) has a simple zero exactly when \(d\mid\ell\), giving the stated pole-order bound. The partition maximum is attained by using as many \(\ell\)-parts as possible and filling the remainder with ones.

value.rationale: The result converts a qualitative rationality observation into an effective degree-local denominator and explicit root-of-unity pole-order envelope. The bound depends only on the multiplicity vector \(p\), not on enumerating tropical curves, so it supplies a reusable consistency check and analytic constraint for fixed-degree all-genus computations. The componentwise exponent is exact at the level of the partition combinatorics, while the statement carefully avoids claiming a minimal denominator after cancellations.
